answer: Because the cedar fee is applied at the ledge exit, the pearl audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake burns a 10% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 13 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
